extra.message: Hardcoded Admin Credentials — An attacker can login as admin using the default password, gaining unrestricted access to customer PII (including credit card numbers) and system configuration. [verified: Lines 62-63 hardcode admin credentials 'admin'/'admin123' in setup_users(). No compensating controls (e.g., password hashing, forced password change) prevent login via the /login endpoint, granting full access to customer PII.]

Server-Side Template Injection in 404 Error Handler — Remote code execution on the server, full compromise of the application and its data (customer PII, database, secrets). [verified: The 404 handler at line 102-114 directly embeds request.url (attacker-controlled) into the template string via % formatting without any sanitization, then passes it to render_template_string, enabling Jinja2 SSTI. No input validation, escaping, or authentication gate exists on this code path.]

Hardcoded Cryptographic Secrets — An attacker can forge valid JWTs with any claims, bypass authentication, and compromise Flask sessions, potentially gaining admin access and exfiltrating sensitive customer data. [verified: Secrets are hardcoded and used for JWT signing (SECRET_KEY_HMAC, SECRET_KEY_HMAC_2) and Flask session signing (app.secret_key). No input validation or rotation mitigates this; source code access (e.g., via path traversal) allows forging tokens, per the threat model's priority on hardcoded secrets.]
